question: At the end of the year, the Math Club decided to hold an election for which 5 equal officer positions were available. However, 16 candidates were nominated, of whom 7 were past officers. Of all possible elections of the officers, how many will have at least 1 of the past officers?
solution:
The positions are equal, so each outcome is an unordered choice of 5 candidates. There are C(16,5) = (16·15·14·13·12)/(5·4·3·2·1) = 4368 outcomes in total.
An outcome with no past officer must choose all 5 from the 16−7 = 9 other candidates. There are C(9,5) = (9·8·7·6·5)/(5·4·3·2·1) = 126 such outcomes.
Subtracting leaves 4368−126 = 4242 outcomes with at least one past officer.
Final answer: 4242
